definition: Cortana is a discontinued virtual assistant developed by Microsoft and first released in April 2014 that used the Bing search engine to perform tasks such as setting reminders and answering questions for users.
details: Cortana was available in English, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, and Japanese language editions, depending on the software platform and region in which it was used. In 2019, Microsoft began reducing the prevalence of Cortana and converting it from an assistant into different software integrations. It was split from the Windows 10 search bar in April 2019. In January 2020, the Cortana mobile app was removed from certain markets, and on March 31, 2021, the Cortana mobile app was shut down globally. On June 2, 2023, Microsoft announced that support for the Cortana standalone app on Microsoft Windows would end in late 2023 and would be replaced by Microsoft Copilot, an AI chatbot. Support for Cortana in the Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365 mobile apps was discontinued in late 2023.

explainer.lead: Cortana was Microsoft’s virtual assistant for tasks such as setting reminders and answering questions through Bing. First released in April 2014, it was later reduced to separate software integrations and discontinued, making it mainly relevant today to older Microsoft products and workflows.

tiers.eli5: Cortana was like a helper who could write a reminder in your notebook or look up an answer for you. It lived in Microsoft apps and devices and used Bing to find information. Microsoft gradually retired the helper, shutting down its mobile app in 2021 and ending its remaining Windows support in late 2023.
tiers.practitioner: Cortana was applied through Windows 10, standalone mobile and Windows apps, and integrations with Outlook and Microsoft 365 mobile apps. Engineers maintaining older workflows should treat it as a discontinued dependency rather than an available assistant platform. Microsoft announced the standalone Windows app’s replacement as Microsoft Copilot, while Outlook and Microsoft 365 mobile support also ended in late 2023.
tiers.paperLevel: Cortana = a Microsoft virtual assistant, first released in April 2014, that performed user tasks including reminder setting and Bing-backed question answering. Language availability covered English, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, and Japanese editions, varying by platform and region. Its deployment was progressively withdrawn from 2019 onward, ending with Windows and Microsoft mobile-app support in late 2023.

explainer.example: A user could ask Cortana to set a reminder for an appointment, then separately ask it a general question; Cortana would handle the reminder as a task and use Bing for the information request.

explainer.intuition: Cortana acted as a conversational helper between a user and Microsoft services: it could record a requested reminder or use Bing to answer a question. Its role later shifted away from a prominent standalone assistant toward smaller software integrations before being withdrawn.
howItWorks: A user asked Cortana to perform a task or answer a question.
For information requests, Cortana used the Bing search engine.
For supported personal tasks, it carried out actions such as setting reminders.
Language availability depended on the software platform and region.
From 2019 onward, Microsoft reduced Cortana’s presence and phased out its apps and integrations.
explainer.whyItMatters: Cortana illustrates how a virtual assistant can move from operating-system and mobile-app integration to a reduced set of software features and eventual retirement. Its shutdown dates also help distinguish legacy Microsoft workflows from current ones.
misconceptions: Cortana is not still supported as a standalone Windows or mobile assistant.
Cortana and Microsoft Copilot are not the same product; Copilot was named as its replacement.
Its eight language editions were not uniformly available across every platform and region.
